requirements.requirement: Restore an executable, legacy-compatible /srv/legacy2/mail-filter-routing/bin/deliver that reads one RFC822 message from standard input.
requirements.summary: The executable was replaced with a POSIX /bin/sh implementation, passed shell syntax validation, consumed sample messages through stdin, and remained executable and functional after restart.

requirements.requirement: Route accounts messages to Maildir/accounts/new, support messages to Maildir/support/new, and all others to Maildir/general/new, matching X-Department header names case-insensitively.
requirements.summary: Direct deliveries reached all three required mailboxes. The lowercase x-department support sample and conventionally cased X-Department accounts sample both routed correctly; the implementation also directly shows header-name normalization with tolower().

requirements.requirement: Leave every delivered message byte-for-byte intact.
requirements.summary: SHA-256 hashes of delivered accounts, support, and general messages exactly matched their source sample hashes.

requirements.requirement: Keep messages with repeated subjects as separate deliveries.
requirements.summary: Delivering the same general sample twice produced two distinct files with identical content hashes, demonstrating separate deliveries despite the repeated subject and content.

requirements.requirement: Retain all staged sample messages unchanged.
requirements.summary: All three samples remained present with hashes matching the preparation baseline, including after the node restart.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: Alpine 3.23.3 and kernel 6.18.7-0-lts were unchanged from after-prepare through after-executor. The solution uses available POSIX shell utilities and executed successfully before and after restart.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. The mandatory node-restart protocol is also complete and coherent: healthy pre-restart state and boot ID were captured, restart was acknowledged, the connection disruption was observed, a different boot ID appeared, and the entry point, stored mail, samples, platform, and fresh delivery behavior recovered. Fixed lifecycle boot identities independently confirm the transition.
limitations: Automated failed-service collection was unsupported because systemctl is unavailable on this Alpine node; this does not materially weaken verification of the standalone mail entry point.

Case-insensitive matching was behaviorally tested with two header-name casings rather than every possible capitalization, with the remaining assurance supplied by direct inspection of the tolower()-based implementation.
Requirement retain-samples cited unknown evidence IDs: seeded-state-node1

operational_hygiene.summary: State-changing actions were appropriately limited to restoring the entry point, making it executable, creating bounded delivery evidence, and performing the mandatory restart and recovery test. The sole unnecessary mutation was /tmp/antrieb-reboot.log, created by the restart command and still present after execution; it was not reverted, but is low-risk temporary residue. No new listeners or package damage were observed.
